parameters.content:
## B · User-loan matching
**Triggers**
- **Webhook** `POST /webhook/ingest-complete` (header secret, private network) right after a CSV is ingested.
- **Sweeper** every 10 min: recovers jobs whose webhook was missed (n8n down, network blip), and runs that matched but never recorded their emails (proved again, then C finishes them).
- **From A** (product mode): re-match all users against new/changed products.

**Claim** = atomic lock on the job, so duplicates and concurrent triggers never double-match. Then **B1** runs the Treasure Hunt, **C** notifies, and products whose criteria compiled late are re-matched for every user (product mode, never loops).

nodes.notes: Manual trigger: matches the newest unmatched upload.

nodes.notes: Called by the ingest Lambda after COMMIT; Header Auth; answers at once.

nodes.notes: Recovery: picks up jobs whose webhook was missed or whose run died.

nodes.notes: Re-match every user against new or changed products.

parameters.query:
-- Workflow B · Sweeper (every 10 min): which upload jobs need a matching run now.
-- No params. Also closes ghost runs. Shared with tests/integration (same file, same SQL).
--
-- A job is picked when it completed ingest and:
--   * was never matched (webhook missed: n8n down, network blip), or
--   * its run died holding the lock (RUNNING for > 15 min), or
--   * its run FAILED (a transient DB/LLM error) and it has failed fewer than 3 times, the
--     last failure at least 10 minutes ago (bounded retry with backoff; after 3 it stays
--     FAILED for a human to look at, and Workflow E has already alerted).
WITH dead AS (  -- n8n's hard timeout is 10 min: a run still 'running' after 30 is dead
  UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status = 'failed', finished_at = now(),
         error = 'abandoned: still running after 30 min (n8n restart or timeout)'
  WHERE status = 'running' AND started_at < now() - interval '30 minutes'
  RETURNING 1
), failures AS (
  SELECT job_id, count(*) AS n, max(coalesce(finished_at, started_at)) AS last_at
  FROM pipeline_runs WHERE status = 'failed' AND job_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY job_id
)
SELECT 'upload' AS mode, j.job_id::text AS job_id, '' AS product_ids
FROM upload_jobs j LEFT JOIN failures f USING (job_id)
WHERE j.status = 'COMPLETED'
  AND (j.match_status IS NULL
       OR (j.match_status = 'RUNNING' AND j.match_started_at < now() - interval '15 minutes')
       OR (j.match_status = 'FAILED' AND coalesce(f.n, 0) < 3 AND f.last_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'))
ORDER BY j.completed_at
LIMIT 5;

nodes.name: Jobs waiting for matching
nodes.notes: sweeper.sql: missed, stale or failed jobs (max 3 tries).

nodes.name: Products → request
nodes.notes: Turns A's product ids into a product-mode request.

parameters.query:
-- Workflow B · Claim a job and start a run. Params: $1 mode ('upload'|'products'),
-- $2 job_id (uuid text or ''), $3 product ids (JSON array text or '').
-- Atomic: only ONE run per job, even with a duplicate webhook + the sweeper racing.
-- 0 rows returned = nothing to do (already matched / running / unknown / out of retries).
-- The retry rule matches sweeper.sql: a FAILED job is reclaimable fewer than 3 times.
WITH req AS (
  SELECT $1::text AS mode, nullif($2, '')::uuid AS job_id, nullif($3, '')::jsonb AS product_ids
), failures AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS n FROM pipeline_runs
  WHERE status = 'failed' AND job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM req)
), locked AS (
  UPDATE upload_jobs j SET match_status = 'RUNNING', match_started_at = now()
  FROM req
  WHERE req.mode = 'upload' AND j.job_id = req.job_id AND j.status = 'COMPLETED'
    AND (j.match_status IS NULL
         OR (j.match_status = 'RUNNING' AND j.match_started_at < now() - interval '15 minutes')
         OR (j.match_status = 'FAILED' AND (SELECT n FROM failures) < 3))
  RETURNING j.job_id
), abandoned AS (  -- a re-claimed job's previous run died: close it (data-modifying CTEs always run)
  UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status = 'failed', finished_at = now(),
         error = 'abandoned: job re-claimed after a stale lock'
  WHERE status = 'running' AND job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM locked)
  RETURNING 1
)
INSERT INTO pipeline_runs (mode, job_id, scope_product_ids)
SELECT req.mode, (SELECT job_id FROM locked),
       CASE WHEN req.mode = 'products'
            THEN ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(req.product_ids))::uuid[] END
FROM req
WHERE req.mode = 'products' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM locked)
RETURNING run_id::text, mode, job_id::text;

nodes.name: Claim job + start run
nodes.notes: Atomic claim: a duplicate webhook racing the sweeper can never double-match.

nodes.name: Match (B1)
nodes.notes: Runs the Treasure Hunt for this run (sub-workflow B1).

nodes.name: Matching failed?
nodes.notes: A failed or stopped B1 run marks the job FAILED instead of hanging.

parameters.query:
WITH run AS (
  UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status = 'failed', finished_at = now(), error = left($2, 2000)
  WHERE run_id = $1::uuid RETURNING job_id
)
UPDATE upload_jobs SET match_status = 'FAILED'
WHERE job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
RETURNING job_id::text

nodes.name: Mark job failed
nodes.notes: Visible in the upload UI; the sweeper retries it later.

nodes.name: Notify users (C)
nodes.notes: Emails users with new matches (sub-workflow C).

parameters.query:
-- Workflow B · Sweeper, second task: runs that wrote their matches but never recorded their
-- emails, because n8n lost its database or restarted between Stage 3 and Workflow C (found live:
-- the job showed "matched" and the screen waited for emails forever). No params.
--
-- Picked: a run with new matches, no email counters, whose proofs did not fail, that either
-- finished more than 15 minutes ago (C normally ends within a few minutes of B1) or was closed as
-- abandoned by the sweeper. Workflow B re-runs the post-write proof first and only then calls C,
-- which is idempotent: users already emailed are skipped, nobody gets two emails.
SELECT r.run_id::text AS run_id
FROM pipeline_runs r
WHERE r.matches_new > 0
  AND r.emails_sent IS NULL
  AND coalesce(r.prewrite_ok, true) AND coalesce(r.correctness_ok, true)
  AND r.started_at > now() - interval '1 day'
  AND (   (r.status = 'done'   AND r.finished_at < now() - interval '15 minutes')
       OR (r.status = 'failed' AND r.error LIKE 'abandoned%'))
ORDER BY r.started_at
LIMIT 2;

nodes.name: Runs waiting for emails
nodes.notes: Runs that wrote matches but never recorded emails (n8n died mid-run).

parameters.query:
-- Correctness proof for the Treasure Hunt (PLAN.md §11.9).
-- Params: $1 run_id, $2 prompt_version.
--
-- Re-decides EVERY user x product pair the naive way: real values, no classes, no floors,
-- one row per pair. Then compares with what the optimized pipeline produced (class
-- decisions expanded to users). The optimization is correct iff the two sets are identical.
WITH run AS (
    SELECT * FROM pipeline_runs WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
), prods AS (
    SELECT p.*, r.rules AS residual_rules, r.requirements AS residual_requirements
    FROM loan_products p
    LEFT JOIN criteria_rules r
           ON r.prompt_version = $2
          AND r.criteria_text_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex')
    WHERE p.is_active
      AND ((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'upload' OR p.product_id = ANY (coalesce((SELECT scope_product_ids FROM run), ARRAY[]::uuid[])))
), usr AS (
    SELECT u.* FROM users u
    WHERE (SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products' OR u.upload_job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
), naive AS (  -- every user x every product, decided on the user's REAL values
    SELECT u.user_id, p.product_id,
        CASE
            WHEN NOT ((p.min_monthly_income IS NULL OR u.monthly_income >= p.min_monthly_income)
                  AND (p.min_credit_score   IS NULL OR u.credit_score  >= p.min_credit_score)
                  AND (p.max_credit_score   IS NULL OR u.credit_score  <= p.max_credit_score)
                  AND (p.min_age            IS NULL OR u.age           >= p.min_age)
                  AND (p.max_age            IS NULL OR u.age           <= p.max_age)
                  AND (p.employment_types   IS NULL OR u.employment_status = ANY (p.employment_types)))
                THEN 'fails_hard_criteria'
            WHEN p.other_criteria_text IS NULL THEN 'eligible'
            WHEN p.residual_rules IS NULL THEN 'conditional'
            WHEN NOT (SELECT coalesce(bool_and(CASE
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.monthly_income >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.monthly_income <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.credit_score  >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.credit_score  <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.age           >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.age           <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        ELSE true END), true)
                      FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p.residual_rules, '[]'::jsonb)) AS x
                      WHERE x->>'applies_to' IN ('any', u.employment_status))
                THEN 'not_eligible'
            WHEN jsonb_array_length(p.residual_requirements) > 0 THEN 'conditional'
            ELSE 'eligible' END AS tier
    FROM usr u CROSS JOIN prods p
), naive_kept AS (
    SELECT user_id, product_id, tier FROM naive WHERE tier IN ('eligible', 'conditional')
), optimized AS (  -- what the pipeline stored for this run
    SELECT m.user_id, m.product_id, m.tier
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.status = 'active' AND m.user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM usr)
      AND m.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM prods)
), diff AS (
    (SELECT * FROM naive_kept EXCEPT SELECT * FROM optimized)
    UNION ALL
    (SELECT * FROM optimized EXCEPT SELECT * FROM naive_kept)
)
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET correctness_ok = ((SELECT count(*) FROM diff) = 0)
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM naive) AS naive_pairs_evaluated,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM naive_kept) AS naive_matches,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM optimized) AS optimized_matches,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM diff) AS mismatches,
    correctness_ok;

nodes.name: Prove again before emailing
nodes.notes: Re-checks every pair of that run before anyone is emailed.

nodes.name: Proof still passes?
nodes.notes: Only an exact run is emailed; a failed proof leaves it for a human.

parameters.query:
-- Workflow B · A recovered run passed its proof again: record it as done before C emails it.
-- Params: $1 run_id.
UPDATE pipeline_runs
SET status = 'done', finished_at = coalesce(finished_at, now()),
    error = CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 'recovered by the sweeper: proof re-run, emails sent'
                 ELSE error END
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id::text, status, correctness_ok;

nodes.name: Mark run recovered
nodes.notes: Records the run as done, noting the sweeper recovered it.

nodes.name: Finish emails (C)
nodes.notes: C picks up where it stopped; users already emailed are skipped.

parameters.query:
-- Workflow B · Products whose criteria were compiled for the FIRST time in this run.
-- Params: $1 run_id, $2 prompt_version.
--
-- When the LLM fails to compile a product's criteria, that product counts as "may qualify" for
-- every user (never wrongly eligible) and the text is retried on the next run. Once a later run
-- compiles it, the users matched BEFORE still hold the provisional decision: B re-matches all
-- users against exactly these products (product mode). The follow-up run finds every text
-- cached (rules_compiled = 0), so this never loops.
WITH run AS (
    SELECT * FROM pipeline_runs WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
)
SELECT $1::text AS run_id,
       coalesce(json_agg(DISTINCT p.product_id), '[]'::json) AS product_ids
FROM loan_products p
JOIN criteria_rules r
  ON r.prompt_version = $2
 AND r.criteria_text_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex')
WHERE p.is_active
  AND coalesce((SELECT rules_compiled FROM run), 0) > 0
  AND r.created_at >= (SELECT started_at FROM run)
  -- a product-mode run already re-decided every user for its own products
  AND NOT ((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products'
           AND p.product_id = ANY (coalesce((SELECT scope_product_ids FROM run), ARRAY[]::uuid[])));

nodes.name: Products compiled late
nodes.notes: Products whose criteria compiled for the first time in this run.

nodes.name: Re-match them?
nodes.notes: Earlier users hold a provisional 'may qualify' for them: decide again.

nodes.name: Re-match all users (B, product mode)
nodes.notes: Product-mode run for those products; it compiles nothing, so it never loops.

meta.description: Triggered by the ingest webhook (primary), a 10-min sweeper (recovery), or Workflow A (product mode).
